Hi Sophie — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: integrate LLM-driven product recommendations into Acme’s checkout flow with tight latency (p95 < 200ms) and cost target under $0.001/token for production.
- Data constraints: customer privacy (PII redaction), retention limited to 30 days for session logs, want private deployment eventually but open to a hosted POC.
- Traffic profile: ~40 tps peak during promos, typical bursty traffic.

Initial model fit recommendations (based on today's prompts and sample outputs):
- Redwood-2.7b-quant (cost-first): strong 1-shot recommendation quality, best cost/TPS profile for high-throughput scenarios.
- Redwood-13b-ptq (balanced): better long-form consistency and handling of product catalogs; recommend for safety/QA-sensitive flows.
- Llama-2-70b (sparsely for high-quality fallback): use as a fallback for critical flows where quality trumps cost.

Immediate next steps:
1) I attached an ACME requirements summary (acme-reqs-summary.xlsx) and a short eval prompt set to validate model fit.
2) We’ll share Redwood-verified benchmark links and a short runbook for running the eval harness against your sample dataset.
3) If metrics look good, propose a 2-week POC (hosted) with a canary route for production-like traffic.

Could you confirm the sample data cadence (how many sessions/day you can share for the eval) and whether you want the POC hosted or private?

I’ll follow up with the benchmark links and a short note on the latency/TPS profiles we saw in our internal tests.

Best,

Thanks Sophie — great questions. Below are the benchmark highlights and links; I’ve also attached a short Redwood-verified PDF summary for ACME. Full Drive folder with raw harness results is linked at the bottom.

Redwood-verified performance profiles (internal lab, p4d-equivalent, 1k-token context unless otherwise noted):
- Redwood-2.7b-quant: 120 TPS (requests/sec), median latency 50ms, p95 140ms, p99 260ms. Cost: lowest of the recommended models. Ideal for high-throughput short prompts.
- Redwood-13b-ptq: 28 TPS, median latency 120ms, p95 240ms, p99 480ms. Better quality for catalog/context-sensitive prompts.
- Llama-2-70b (fallback): ~6 TPS at 1k tokens, median 420ms, p95 1.1s, p99 1.9s — use selectively as a high-quality fallback.

Cold-start vs warm-start / KV cache notes:
- Prefix/KV cache yields ~2–4x latency improvement on repeated session flows once warmed (depends on sequence-length variance). Our harness includes warm-start runs — see folder.
- We can enable session affinity on the Hosted POC to maximize cache hit rate for your checkout sessions.

Prompt set & evaluation artifacts:
- Shared prompt set (sanitized) in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood/ACME-benchmarks
- Attached: redwood-verified-benchmarks-acme-20260715.pdf (summary of TPS/latency percentiles, token-cost estimates, and recommended quantization profiles).
- Raw harness results (CSV + plot) are in the Drive folder for your data team to review.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Your team confirms the sample traffic cadence (you mentioned 5k sessions/day — that works).
2) We drop the sanitized prompt set into your S3/Drive and you run the privacy checks; we recommend writing a short redaction script (we can share a starter).
3) Kick off a hosted POC: 2 weeks, canary route + monitoring dashboards (we’ll include per-route latency and token cost breakdowns).

Pricing note: I’ll include a rough hosted POC estimate in the follow-up (depends on retention, token throughput). If helpful, I can include a cost comparison table for Redwood-2.7b-quant vs 13b-ptq.

Links & artifacts:
- Drive (prompt set + raw harness): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood/ACME-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-2026-01

Let me know if you want the cost table in this thread or as a quick follow-up doc.

Best,
